title: GPU Fleet Capacity & Networking: IaC / CI-CD Operational Guidelines (2026)
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Summary:

This operational guideline consolidates best practices, runbooks, and IaC patterns for managing Redwood's GPU fleet, cloud accounts, and networking configuration. It describes capacity planning targets, Terraform module usage, CI/CD pipeline expectations, and runbook steps for the most common operational scenarios.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: Infra engineers, SRE, platform owners, and on-call responders.
- Scope: GPU fleet capacity management, cloud accounts & networking for inference clusters, Terraform/IaC module conventions, CI/CD for infra modules and GPU images, and runbook playbooks for incidents and maintenance.

Goals and SLOs:
- Maintain fleet-wide GPU availability >= 99.9% (monthly).
- Median pod startup latency for inference nodes <= 120s after scale-up.
- Target average GPU utilization: 60-70% (operational window). Avoid sustained >85% to prevent degraded performance.
- Autoscaler responsiveness: scale-up when node-backed queue backlog > 80% capacity for 120s; scale-down when utilization <30% for 10m.

Ownership:
- Service owner: infra/gpu-fleet (team lead: @aisha-khan).
- Runtime components: gpu-scheduler, capacity-manager, gpu-metrics-exporter (owned by infra-serving).
- IaC modules: infra-iac-modules (module owners listed in module READMEs).

Architecture overview (high level):
- GPU Fleet sits in dedicated VPCs per cloud account (prod/staging/dev).
- Each region has a fleet control-plane: gpu-scheduler (k8s operator), capacity-manager (autoscaler), and image-builder pipelines.
- Networking uses private subnets + NAT egress for image pulls and metrics ingestion; peering to central logging/observability VPCs.

Capacity planning & forecasting:
1. Data sources:
   - gpu-metrics-exporter (per-node GPU utilization, memory, temperature).
   - cluster-queue-length metrics (pending pod count labeled by priority).
   - billing & reserved instance utilization from cloud accounts.
2. Forecast cadence:
   - Weekly rolling lookbacks (7/30/90d) used by capacity planning dashboard.
   - Quarterly capacity planning cycle triggered 6 weeks before expected demand increases (e.g., new model rollouts, enterprise customer onboarding).
3. Policy thresholds:
   - Emergency scale threshold: sustained cluster GPU utilization >85% for 10m -> notify on-call and start scale-up plan.
   - Normal scale-up trigger: pending queue >80% of provisioning capacity for 2m -> autoscaler adds nodes.
   - Scale-down: per-node GPU utilization <30% and queue <20% for 10m -> eligible for graceful drain.
4. Safety cushions:
   - Maintain 10% buffer of reserved capacity for high-tier customers (Dedicated).
   - Maintain at least one warm spare node group per region to avoid cold-start delays.

Networking & cloud accounts (practical config):
- Account layout:
  - accounts: org-prod-gpu, org-staging-gpu, org-dev-gpu (separate billing and IAM boundaries).
  - Central services account: org-shared-logging, org-shared-observability.
- VPC topology:
  - Public LB subnets (for managed load-balancers), private worker subnets, NAT subnets for outbound.
  - Peering: region-level peering from gpu VPCs to shared-services VPC. Use route tables with explicit route propagation.
- Security groups / firewall rules:
  - Allow cluster control-plane (port 6443) only from admin CIDRs and central control-plane account.
  - Worker nodes: allow outbound 443 to registries and 9090/9300 to observability endpoints.
  - Disable broad 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on worker security groups.
- Egress & proxies:
  - Use central egress NAT + TLS inspection for approved registries.
  - Use signed images from internal registry (image_signer pipeline).

Terraform / IaC module conventions:
- Module naming: infra-iac-modules/<domain>/<purpose> (e.g., infra-iac-modules/gpu/instance-pool).
- Versioning: semantic versions; pin module versions in environment-specific repos.
- Patterns:
  - Inputs-only modules (no implicit external state changes).
  - Outputs: export IDs, IPs, service-account emails, and module version used.
  - Module maturity labels: alpha/beta/stable in module README.
- Key modules (examples):
  1. gpu-instance-pool: manages instance group, GPU type, image_family, taints/labels.
  2. gpu-networking: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, peering.
  3. iam-roles-and-bindings: service accounts, KMS access, registry read permissions.
  4. cluster-bootstrap: k8s cluster config, node-pools, cluster-autoscaler config.

Terraform example (snippet):
| Resource | Example input | Note |
|---|---:|---|
| instance_count | 16 | desired initial pool size |
| gpu_type | nvidia-a100-80gb | production default |
| taints | {key="gpu",value="true",effect="NoSchedule"} | enforces scheduling |

Example CLI guardrails:
- terraform plan must run in CI with drift-check job.
- PRs that change gpu-instance-pool module require approval from module owners and infra-sre.

CI/CD & build pipelines:
- Repo layout:
  - infra-modules/* — contains reusable Terraform modules (protected branches).
  - envs/prod, envs/staging — environment overlay repos that compose modules.
  - images/gpu-base — Packer/OS image sources + GPU drivers.
- Pipeline stages (module changes):
  1. Lint & fmt (tflint, terraform fmt).
  2. Unit plan (terraform init/plan in a sandbox).
  3. Integration plan (apply to ephemeral test account using infra-e2e runner).
  4. Approval gates (module owners + infra-sre).
  5. Promote tag and generate release artifact.
- Image build pipeline (images/gpu-base):
  - Build image -> run GPU smoke tests -> sign image -> publish to internal registry.
  - Image rolling update pipeline will create a node-pool with new image, drain & cordon old nodes, and perform canary tests.
- Rollout strategy for infra artifacts:
  - Canary -> Traffic ramp -> Full rollout. Default canary size: 5% traffic / 2 nodes (min 1 zone).
  - Abort criteria: failing smoke tests, increased 99th latency > 20% vs baseline, or elevated OOM/gpu-memory errors.

Runbooks & common incidents:
- Incident: High GPU contention / slow inference
  1. Pager triggers on gpu-fleet-utilization >85% (10m) OR pending pods >100.
  2. On-call: acknowledge and open incident in PagerDuty -> create incident channel.
  3. Run checks: cluster utilization (gpu-metrics-exporter), pending pods by priority, recent deploys (git commits).
  4. Mitigations (ordered):
     a. Temporarily increase autoscaler max nodes for region (use capacity-manager CLI).
     b. Scale up reserved instance pool for high-tier customers if affected.
     c. Deprioritize low-priority batch jobs (apply label schedule=defer via job controller).
     d. If caused by bad rollout, roll back recent model-serving deployment (follow deployment rollback playbook).
  5. Post-incident: run regression triage and update capacity dashboard parameters.

- Incident: Node GPU driver or CUDA regression after image update
  1. Hit: Pod GPU errors / driver mismatch messages in kube events.
  2. Immediate action: cordon affected nodes and drain non-essential pods.
  3. Revert node group to previous signed image and redeploy.
  4. Escalate to platform kernel-driver owner for a postmortem.

Maintenance & upgrade procedure (example: CUDA driver update):
1. Pre-checks:
   - Ensure kernel-driver and nvidia-driver compatibility matrix validated in module README.
   - Run canary image build and smoke tests in staging region.
2. Rollout plan:
   - Create new node-pool with updated image.
   - Run canary jobs: inference smoke (p95 latency), memory/stability tests for 4h.
   - If canary passes, ramp to 25% for 2h, then 60% for 4h, then full rollout.
3. Rollback steps:
   - Cordon and drain new pool, scale up previous image node-pool to replace capacity, update autoscaler groups.

Emergency rollback checklist:
- Preconditions: previous image/tag available in registry, terraform state has previous node-pool counts.
- Steps: manual terraform apply to restore previous node pool sizes and image IDs -> trigger k8s rollout of workloads -> validate smoke tests.

Observability & alerting recommendations:
- Essential metrics:
  - cluster_gpu_utilization (avg/95/99), gpu_memory_pressure, pending_pod_count, node_gpu_errors.
- Alerts & thresholds:
  - P0: cluster_gpu_utilization >90% for 5m -> page.
  - P1: pending_pod_count >200 for 10m -> notify Slack + Ops.
  - P2: node_gpu_errors spike (>=5 in 1m) -> investigate.
- Dashboards: per-region capacity overview, per-customer reserved usage, provisioning latency histogram.

Compliance & auditing:
- Ensure Terraform state is stored in encrypted backend (remote state with KMS).
- Enable audit logging for all role changes and node image promotions.

Appendix: useful commands & snippets
- Check GPU utilization (prometheus):
  - promql: avg_over_time(cluster_gpu_utilization[5m]) by (region)
- Increase autoscaler max (capacity-manager CLI):
  - capacity-manager set-max --region us-west1 --pool gpu-prod-a --max 64
- Terraform drift check (CI):
  - terraform init && terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan | jq .

Related pages:
- infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026 (detailed onboarding)
- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 (incident-focused runbook)

Document maintenance:
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major fleet or networking change.
- Owners: infra/gpu-fleet + infra-platform.

End of document.
